nodes.label: Graphify Context Layer
nodes.rationale: A persistent on-disk knowledge graph queried for context instead of re-reading the codebase each session; additive, so when missing every role falls back to normal reading and the harness never depends on it.

nodes.label: Graph Freshness Maintenance
nodes.rationale: A stale graph misleads, so keep it current: the post-commit hook re-runs deterministic free AST extraction on code, while semantic doc extraction costs tokens and runs on demand via /graphify --update.

nodes.label: graphify query Command
nodes.rationale: Roles prefer graphify query / path / explain over a cold read and quote the returned source_location when citing a fact.

nodes.label: graphify-out/graph.json Graph Data
nodes.rationale: Raw graph data in PROJECT_ROOT/graphify-out/ queried by graphify query, path, and explain; its presence/staleness gates the verifier advisory.

nodes.label: GRAPH_REPORT.md Audit
nodes.rationale: Plain-language audit of god nodes, communities, and surprising edges the leader reads to scope exploration and spot cross-module coupling before delegating.

nodes.label: CI Test Suite Job (Node build + run_tests.sh)
nodes.norm_label: ci test suite job (node build + run_tests.sh)

nodes.label: HARNESS_WORKSPACE Resolution Order
nodes.rationale: Resolution precedence harness.config.json -> feature_list.json config -> .handyman/ -> legacy fallback keeps mutable state out of the repo root while staying discoverable.

nodes.label: Handyman Skill (agent work harness)
nodes.rationale: Core idea: the chat coordinates but the disk is the source of truth; every session has state, backlog, closure criteria and executable verification. Formerly named Foreman.

nodes.label: Local vs Global Install Modes
nodes.rationale: local keeps docs versioned next to code under .handyman/; global moves operational state to $HOME/HANDYMAN/<project> to keep the repo clean.

nodes.label: Anti Telefono Descompuesto Pattern
nodes.rationale: Long agent reports are written to backlog/ files and the chat only returns references, avoiding degradation of information between agents.

nodes.label: Obsidian Vault Integration
nodes.rationale: HARNESS_WORKSPACE opens directly as an Obsidian vault (frontmatter, #handyman/... tags, index.md MOC) without duplicating files.

nodes.label: Determinism Asymmetry (JSON state scripted, markdown artifacts manual)
nodes.rationale: feature_list.json got a deterministic CLI (feature.py) because hand-editing caused split-scope and drift; current.md, history.md and backlog/ entries never received the equivalent, so cross-model format drift persists there.
nodes.norm_label: determinism asymmetry (json state scripted, markdown artifacts manual)

nodes.label: Analisis: actualizar un harness en version antigua
nodes.norm_label: analisis: actualizar un harness en version antigua

nodes.label: Idempotent Version Migrations (upgrade_harness)
nodes.rationale: DB-migration style ordered idempotent steps (1.5->1.6->1.7...) with --check, --dry-run and backup close content drift that re-running scaffold.sh cannot.

nodes.label: Managed Scaffolding vs Project-Owned State
nodes.rationale: The skill may update bridge files, templates, role scaffolding and schemas; it must never overwrite feature_list.json, progress/, backlog/ or filled docs - for those tools only report. This rule prevents upgrades from destroying user work.

nodes.label: Analisis: recoger contexto business en bootstrap
nodes.norm_label: analisis: recoger contexto business en bootstrap

nodes.label: Mandatory Business Interview at Bootstrap
nodes.rationale: docs/business.md is the only core doc that cannot be inferred from code, so bootstrap must actively interview the user (template as interview script + protocol step + placeholder advisory) instead of consuming context passively.

nodes.label: Feature Request Archetypes (Investigacion vs Implementacion)
nodes.rationale: The 24 real features split cleanly into research requests (plan in docs/) and implementation requests (code + tests); the template should encode a core/optional field split and the empirical invariant that the green gate is always the last acceptance bullet.

nodes.label: Analisis: harnesses del ecosistema y features comunes
nodes.norm_label: analisis: harnesses del ecosistema y features comunes

nodes.label: Canonical Harness Core (feature list, progress file, startup ritual, verifier gate)
nodes.rationale: Handyman already implements the full canonical core because it descends from Anthropic's initializer + coding agent pattern; real gaps are dependency graph, unattended loop contract and review depth.
nodes.norm_label: canonical harness core (feature list, progress file, startup ritual, verifier gate)

nodes.label: Ralph Loop (unattended agent while-loop pattern)
nodes.rationale: Handyman has all loop ingredients (disk state, deterministic verifier, single feature) but lacks the loop contract: exit codes meaning drained vs blocked vs verifier failed.

nodes.label: Two-Stage Review (spec compliance then code quality)
nodes.norm_label: two-stage review (spec compliance then code quality)

nodes.label: Analisis: inconsistencia del bootstrap entre modelos
nodes.norm_label: analisis: inconsistencia del bootstrap entre modelos

nodes.label: scaffold.sh as Single Bootstrap Path
nodes.rationale: Bootstrap inconsistency across models is a design property, not a model bug: multiple prose sources of truth disagree with the deterministic script, so all paths must collapse to scaffold.sh + feature.py add.

nodes.label: Live Schema Validation of feature_list.json
nodes.rationale: additionalProperties:false in the schema rejects invented keys like start_date/close_date, but only once the verifier validates the live state instead of only the templates.

nodes.label: Feature List Is a State Machine, Not a Timeline
nodes.rationale: Features carry no dates; chronology lives in progress/current.md and progress/history.md. Making this explicit removes the reasonable hallucination that led models to invent date fields.
nodes.norm_label: feature list is a state machine, not a timeline

nodes.label: Analisis: observador web local de la flota handyman
nodes.norm_label: analisis: observador web local de la flota handyman

nodes.label: Fleet Observer Architecture (disk -> watcher -> Bun.serve -> SSE -> browser)
nodes.rationale: One process, read-only first: serve files as-is, invalidate by watcher+mtime, SSE push, BM25 search in the browser; no new persistence because the harness already persists everything.
nodes.norm_label: fleet observer architecture (disk -> watcher -> bun.serve -> sse -> browser)

nodes.label: Filesystem as Database (Obsidian/sniffly pattern)
nodes.rationale: The registry stores only project_root + date; everything else is read live from each harness's disk - single source of truth with no mirrors that can drift.

nodes.label: Analisis: peticiones a modelos LLM desde TypeScript para toolBox
nodes.norm_label: analisis: peticiones a modelos llm desde typescript para toolbox

nodes.label: Server-Side LLM Relay over SSE (/api/ask)
nodes.rationale: The no-bundler constraint only applies to the browser; all model calls live in toolbox_serve.ts so the browser never sees an API key, and every LLM call is pull or batch (never automatic per SSE event) with results cached by state hash.

nodes.label: Analisis: procesos pre-run y post-run de features
nodes.norm_label: analisis: procesos pre-run y post-run de features

nodes.label: Preflight Stability Gate (scripts/preflight orchestrator)
nodes.rationale: No capability was missing, only orchestration: a thin read-only script calls the five existing checkers (validate/upgrade --check/update --list/tools_discovery check) and reports format/drift/sync/discovery without ever blocking.

nodes.label: post_run Hooks (opt-in extension of feature.py done)
nodes.rationale: A declared post_run command list in harness.config.json runs after closure with exit 0 always; a failing custom step warns but never reverts an already verified close. YAGNI by default, extensibility opt-in.
nodes.norm_label: post_run hooks (opt-in extension of feature.py done)

nodes.label: Analisis: RAG en handyman - estado del arte y opciones
nodes.norm_label: analisis: rag en handyman - estado del arte y opciones

nodes.label: Agentic Search over RAG for Harness State
nodes.rationale: The harness corpus is small, structured and constantly changing - exactly where grep/read agentic search wins and a vector index goes stale; Anthropic removed vector search from Claude Code for the same reason. Recommendation: no RAG pipeline for handyman.
nodes.norm_label: agentic search over rag for harness state

nodes.label: Backlog Deduplication (cheap candidates + LLM judge)
nodes.rationale: The only case with clear embedding ROI: paraphrased duplicates where BM25 fails; design is top-k vector + top-k BM25 fused with RRF, verdict by a cheap LLM judge; below ~500 items BM25 + judge alone suffices.

nodes.label: Analisis y fix: Snyk agent-scan W011
nodes.norm_label: analisis y fix: snyk agent-scan w011

nodes.label: Passive Framing Fix (resource-as-subject rewrite)
nodes.rationale: The problem was lexical, not behavioral: describing ingestion with the agent as grammatical subject triggers the W011 heuristic. Rewriting to resource-as-subject preserves the security guidance intact while guard test test_w011_passive_framing prevents regressions.

nodes.label: Analisis: sprints, cierre de periodo y trabajo multi-rama
nodes.norm_label: analisis: sprints, cierre de periodo y trabajo multi-rama

nodes.label: Sprint as Declared Partition Label, Summary as Derived Artifact
nodes.rationale: sprint: YYYY-SPn is a partition label (not a date, preserving the state-machine rule); the sprint document is generated at close from existing artifacts (feature_list, history headings, backlog frontmatter) and done features are archived so the state machine stays small and alive.
nodes.norm_label: sprint as declared partition label, summary as derived artifact

nodes.label: git worktree for Multi-Branch Parallelism
nodes.rationale: Because .handyman/ is untracked, each worktree gets its own workspace for free; the harness only adds branch provenance in current.md/history and an advisory for the shared-checkout degraded case.

nodes.label: Analisis: tests asociados a las evaluaciones del modelo
nodes.norm_label: analisis: tests asociados a las evaluaciones del modelo

nodes.label: trigger-eval.json (20-query skill trigger eval set)
nodes.rationale: The eval data is well built (balanced, near-miss negatives, bilingual) but had no harness: no structural test, no runner, no advisory - a declared gate never wired as a gate.

nodes.label: Analisis: descubrimiento de skills y MCPs determinista
nodes.norm_label: analisis: descubrimiento de skills y mcps determinista

nodes.label: discovery Block in harness.config.json
nodes.rationale: Optional discovery.skills/mcp arrays declare which tools the harness depends on, enabling deterministic list/find/check verification; schema-first because additionalProperties:false rejects undeclared keys.

nodes.label: Semantic Platform Discovery vs Deterministic Harness Contract
nodes.rationale: Skill triggering (description matching) and tool_search similarity remain platform heuristics; the harness can only declare intent and verify presence - it wraps semantic discovery in a declared, verifiable contract without replacing it.
nodes.norm_label: semantic platform discovery vs deterministic harness contract

nodes.label: Analisis: discovery de agentes y referencias de herramientas
nodes.norm_label: analisis: discovery de agentes y referencias de herramientas

nodes.label: discovery.agents Extension (consulting agents as third tool class)
nodes.rationale: Agents are files on disk (.github/agents, .claude/agents) so their verification is as reliable as skills; the extension reuses _parse_frontmatter and PLATFORM_ROLE_DIRS instead of new machinery.
nodes.norm_label: discovery.agents extension (consulting agents as third tool class)

nodes.label: Portable Contract (names) vs Local Resolution (paths)
nodes.rationale: The discovery block stores names because it travels with the repo; paths are machine-specific and derivable at query time, so check/list expose resolved paths but never persist them in the contract.

nodes.label: Analisis: mejoras de UI del observador toolBox
nodes.norm_label: analisis: mejoras de ui del observador toolbox

nodes.label: --hw-* Design Tokens (taller digital palette, WCAG-AA)
nodes.rationale: The legacy UX analyses already settled the design system; any UI improvement must consume the existing tokens, never add loose hex values.

nodes.label: Safe Markdown Rendering (marked + DOMPurify UMD)
nodes.rationale: react-markdown is ESM-only and unusable without a bundler; marked + DOMPurify with FORBID_TAGS/ATTR and CSP default-src 'self' treats agent-authored content as untrusted even though it is local.

nodes.label: Seven-Stage Feature Pipeline (0 estabilidad ... 6 cierre)
nodes.rationale: Stages already exist de facto, each with a deterministic guardian and a dated artifact on disk; the golden rule is 'a stage without its artifact did not happen'. Granularity comes from artifacts, never from widening the 4-state enum.

nodes.label: scripts/metrics (read-only aggregator of history/backlog/feature_list)
nodes.rationale: All existing deterministic observations photograph the present; metrics is the missing historical reader deriving throughput, first-pass approval rate and report coverage from artifacts the workflow already stamps.

nodes.label: Estado de la migracion Python+Bash -> TypeScript/Node
nodes.norm_label: estado de la migracion python+bash -> typescript/node

nodes.label: Strangler Fig Migration Strategy
nodes.rationale: One Python script ported to TS at a time; invariants that cannot break: CLI surface, exit codes (0/1/2 usage/3 ready), stdout shape (status: ok|warn|error + next:), state file bytes, one feature at a time.

nodes.label: Parity Oracle (black-box bash suites repointed to node dist)
nodes.rationale: The existing tests/test_*.sh suites act as parity oracle: repoint to node dist/x.js without editing assertions, plus byte-to-byte fixture-twin comparison, so each port proves equivalence for free.
nodes.norm_label: parity oracle (black-box bash suites repointed to node dist)

nodes.label: handyman/src/core Shared Module (diff, frontmatter, featureList, schema, workspace)
nodes.norm_label: handyman/src/core shared module (diff, frontmatter, featurelist, schema, workspace)

nodes.label: toolbox_serve.ts (read-only web observer, SSE + React UMD + MiniSearch)
nodes.norm_label: toolbox_serve.ts (read-only web observer, sse + react umd + minisearch)

nodes.label: Mapa de entidades de negocio - Handyman
nodes.norm_label: mapa de entidades de negocio - handyman

nodes.label: Feature Entity (id, name, status, acceptance, sprint, depends_on)
nodes.norm_label: feature entity (id, name, status, acceptance, sprint, depends_on)

nodes.label: Agent Roles (leader / implementer / reviewer / explorer)
nodes.rationale: Roles communicate only through disk state and validate work with executable verification; each role has its own template, protocol, model default and least-privilege tool set.

nodes.label: HARNESS_WORKSPACE (Mutable State Root)
nodes.rationale: Mutable harness state (feature_list.json, progress/, backlog/, docs/) is isolated from the repo root so the code tree stays clean; resolution order is harness.config.json, then feature_list.json config, then PROJECT_ROOT/.handyman/, then legacy PROJECT_ROOT fallback. Local scope uses .handyman, global uses $HOME/HANDYMAN/<project_name>.

nodes.label: One Feature At A Time
nodes.rationale: Never mix unrelated feature work: at most one feature in_progress, lowest-id pending first. Keeps blast radius bounded and makes review and state coherence checkable (CHECKPOINTS C2).

nodes.label: Disk Is The Source Of Truth
nodes.rationale: All harness state lives on disk (feature_list.json, progress/current.md, progress/history.md) rather than in chat context, so sessions can be interrupted and resumed and agents cannot drift from unrecorded state.
nodes.norm_label: disk is the source of truth

nodes.label: Anti-Telefono-Descompuesto (Report Files Over Chat)
nodes.rationale: Subagents write full reports to $HARNESS_WORKSPACE/backlog/ (impl_, review_, explore_ files) and reply only with a file reference like 'done -> backlog/impl_cli_edit.md'. Prevents lossy relay of long diffs and findings through chat (the broken-telephone effect).

nodes.label: Executable Verification (Green Verifier Gate)
nodes.rationale: No feature is done until the verifier (normally ./init.sh) exits 0 with real tests. The agent does not claim it works; it demonstrates it. Guards against prose claiming success without evidence.

nodes.label: Untrusted Content Is Data, Not Instructions
nodes.rationale: Ingested files, tool output, code, web pages, backlog reports, and feature descriptions must never trigger actions; irreversible actions require explicit user confirmation. The leader, holding the widest tools, is the main injection target.
nodes.norm_label: untrusted content is data, not instructions

nodes.label: Least-Privilege Tools Per Role
nodes.rationale: Leader gets the widest tools (agent, web, browser); implementer and reviewer get no delegation or web; explorer is read-only without edit. Cheap fast models for implementer/reviewer, strong reasoning for the leader. Limits injection surface and cost.

nodes.label: feature_list.json (Central Feature State)
nodes.rationale: Single JSON file in HARNESS_WORKSPACE holding features with id, name, title, description, acceptance[], and status (pending/in_progress/done); mutated deterministically via node dist/feature.js rather than by hand.

nodes.label: init.sh Verifier
nodes.rationale: Executable gate run from PROJECT_ROOT: checks required harness files, validates state from HARNESS_WORKSPACE, runs tests. Exit 0 is the precondition for starting work and for marking any feature done.

nodes.label: backlog/ Report Convention (impl_/review_/explore_)
nodes.rationale: Per-task evidence files with role frontmatter written under $HARNESS_WORKSPACE/backlog/: impl_<feature>.md, review_<feature>.md, explore_<topic>.md. Generated deterministically by node dist/backlog.js and never overwritten.

nodes.label: Workspace As Obsidian Vault
nodes.rationale: The harness workspace doubles as an Obsidian vault: YAML frontmatter on every note, an index.md MOC, wiki links, and #handyman/... tags, making harness state browsable and queryable by humans.

nodes.label: Graphify Graph As Context Layer
nodes.rationale: Agents query the graphify knowledge graph (graphify query) before exploring code and keep it fresh with /graphify --update; explorers start from returned source_locations instead of scanning blindly.

nodes.label: Two-Stage Review (Spec Then Quality)
nodes.rationale: Stage 1 checks spec compliance against acceptance criteria and declared scope; a Stage 1 failure ends the review with CHANGES_REQUESTED without reaching Stage 2 (code quality), so spec drift is never buried under style feedback.

nodes.label: Feature Request Archetypes (Research vs Implementation)
nodes.rationale: Every request picks an archetype: [Research] leaves a plan in docs/, [Implementation] changes code plus tests. One request equals one feature; the green gate is always the last acceptance bullet; only name/title/description/acceptance become the feature_list.json entry.

nodes.label: Bootstrap Business Interview
nodes.rationale: docs/business.md must be filled during bootstrap by interviewing the user, never by inferring the domain from code, because the domain, stakeholders, and rules usually live only in the user's head. Bootstrap is incomplete until the file reflects real business context.

nodes.label: Role Files As Bridge Files
nodes.rationale: Agent/role files always live in platform-discoverable paths (.github/agents/ or .claude/agents/), never inside HARNESS_WORKSPACE, because the host only loads agents from those known paths; placing them in the workspace makes them undiscoverable and uninvocable.

nodes.label: Seven-Stage Feature Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Each stage (0-6 plus period close 7) has a deterministic guardian and leaves a dated artifact on disk; measures are derived from artifacts, never declared in the contract. Rule: a stage without its artifact did not happen.

nodes.label: Stability Check (preflight)
nodes.rationale: preflight.js orchestrates six controls (format, contract, version drift, config-role sync, discovery, worklist) but always exits 0: it reports stability rather than gating, because the blocking checks already live in the verifier's validate phase.

nodes.label: scaffold.sh (deterministic scaffold)
nodes.rationale: scaffold.sh is the canonical way to lay down the file set and writes harness.config.json in both scopes; snippets exist only for filling content, because re-creating the layout by hand is the main cause of cross-model drift.

nodes.label: feature-request.md Intake Form
nodes.rationale: Only name/title/description/acceptance become the feature_list.json entry; process-guidance sections are never stored keys, and the green gate is always the last acceptance bullet, mirroring how every closed feature ends its acceptance.

nodes.label: update_harness Updater CLI
nodes.source_location: Updating Models In An Existing Harness
nodes.rationale: Model names rotate; the updater edits the models/tools maps in harness.config.json and the frontmatter of every discovered role file in the same run so surfaces never drift apart.

nodes.label: Progressive Disclosure (skill loading)
nodes.source_location: How the platform discovers skills and MCPs
nodes.rationale: Only a skill's name and description sit in context; the body loads when the task matches. The description is therefore the trigger: a skill that describes itself poorly is simply not found.

nodes.label: discovery Block In harness.config.json
nodes.rationale: The block records names, never paths: names are portable intent that travels with the repo, while paths are machine-specific and resolved at query time. Deliver the path, do not store it. It is optional and global because skills/MCPs/agents are mostly cross-role.

nodes.label: tools_discovery CLI (list/find/check/declare)
nodes.rationale: The reproducible counterpart of the host's semantic discovery: skill roots scan local-first-then-global so a vendored skill shadows a global one; check gates on missing skills/agents but only NOTEs absent MCP servers because MCP availability is host-defined.

nodes.label: Deterministic vs Semantic Discovery Boundary
nodes.rationale: Handyman does not replace the platform's semantic discovery but wraps it in a declared, verifiable contract: the discovery block plus schemas plus the CLI are deterministic; the actual skill trigger and tool_search similarity stay semantic. The harness can declare and verify presence but cannot force a trigger.

nodes.label: Trigger Eval Set (evals/trigger-eval.json)
nodes.rationale: A balanced set of labeled queries with negatives written as near-misses: near-misses share vocabulary with the skill but ask for something else, which is what catches a description that over-triggers.

nodes.label: evals CLI (validate/measure)
nodes.rationale: validate is offline and gates; measure needs a runner and degrades to a NOTE with exit 0 when absent, so the stochastic half never blocks CI.

nodes.label: Deterministic Contract vs Stochastic Measurement
nodes.rationale: The eval-set contract is deterministic (same file, same answer) and safe to gate; the real trigger is model-dependent and drifts between runs, so it is measured, never asserted. Confusing the two makes the gate flaky, while leaning only on the size cap mistakes 'the description fits' for 'the description triggers'.

nodes.label: pass@k Completion Reliability
nodes.rationale: Derived from already-measured trigger rates as 1-(1-r)^k with no extra model calls; unlike a confusion matrix it exposes reliability under retry, the property that matters when the skill loads inside a long-running harness. Variance (mean +/- stddev over --runs) and a held-out split guard against noise and overfitting the wording.

nodes.label: Persistent Knowledge Graph (graphify-out/)
nodes.rationale: An additive context layer: agents query a persistent on-disk graph instead of re-reading the codebase each session; every edge is tagged EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS so agents can weigh trust. When the graph is missing every role falls back to normal reading, so the harness never depends on it.

nodes.label: Workspace As Obsidian Vault
nodes.source_location: Open The Workspace As A Vault
nodes.rationale: HARNESS_WORKSPACE doubles as an Obsidian vault without duplicating files: the same markdown agents read and write powers the visual workspace; Obsidian only adds visualization, search, backlinks, and tag navigation.

nodes.label: index.md Map Of Content (MOC)
nodes.rationale: Regenerated from live state with node dist/index_md.js; it links only files that exist and uses wikilinks for vault-internal targets so the verifier's link check stays green. Repo-root bridge files sit outside the vault and are referenced as plain paths.

nodes.label: Indirect Prompt Injection
nodes.rationale: Disk as source of truth means most context is text no one in the session authored; routing outside content into context is the point of the harness but also the injection path. Medium risk in the single-user supervised case, rising with team size, global installs, untrusted PRs, and web access.

nodes.label: ToolBox Live Observer (toolbox serve)
nodes.rationale: Pull, read-only, observe-don't-gate: a localhost-only web panel (disk -> fs.watch -> SSE -> browser) with hard 127.0.0.1 bind, Host-header check, GET-only, registry as read allowlist, and React text-only rendering so harness text never becomes markup. No foreign verifier runs unless --run-verifier is passed.

nodes.label: ToolBox Heartbeat (post_run closure event)
nodes.rationale: A drop-in post_run hook appending closure events to events.jsonl; feature done treats a failing post_run step as a warning, so a missing toolBox script never blocks a verified closure. timeline merges events with history, preferring history on collisions.

nodes.label: Client-Side BM25 Search (observer #/search)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately client-side retrieval: the RAG analysis concluded the harness corpus needs no server-side RAG pipeline — a BM25 index (MiniSearch) rebuilt from disk in milliseconds is immune to staleness, and agents keep using agentic search.
